_comment: Example of config.json in the settings directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/xencode`, or `~/.xencode` before a migration). Copy it there, or set individual keys with `xencode config set <KEY> <VALUE>`. `XCODE_CONFIG_DIR` points every kind of file at one directory instead. Only the keys below exist — unknown keys are ignored by the loader. Cloud providers are selected by model prefix: `qwen:...`, `google_gemini:...`, or an OpenRouter-style `vendor/model` id; the local model is `default_model`. A `remote:` prefix (any OpenAI-compatible server, including one the Colab bridge tunnels to your laptop) uses `remote_base_url` + `api_keys.remote_api_key`. The `colab` block configures `xencode colab up`; a successful bring-up rewrites `llama_cpp_url` (or `ollama_url`) and `remote_base_url` to point at the local forward. `agent_fallback_models` is tried in order by the agent, only while nothing has streamed yet; a `vendor/model` entry needs `openrouter_api_key`. Cloud routes are switched off until `allow_cloud_models` is true — a key in `api_keys` identifies you to a provider, it does not permit the trip. Each credential is looked for in three places, in this order: the value stored here, then a command reference (write `command:secret-tool lookup service xencode` and only that command is kept on disk — its output is the key, and neither the key nor its value is ever printed back), then the provider's environment variable (`API_KEY_OPENAI`, `API_KEY_OPENROUTER`, `API_KEY_GEMINI`, `API_KEY_QWEN`, `XENCODE_API_KEY` or `API_KEY_REMOTE` for `remote:` only, `NVIDIA_NIM_API_KEY` or `API_KEY_NVIDIA`). Setting a credential to a blank value unsets it. `allow_online_docs` is a separate switch for the agent's `read_docs` tool: with it off, a crate's documentation is read only from the copy cargo already unpacked on this machine; with it on, `read_docs` may fetch the version-pinned readme from crates.io or docs.rs when there is no local copy. `layout` names the body arrangement: the shipped `classic`, `chat-first` or `zen`, or a name declared in `layout_templates`, which holds template trees (a leaf naming a slot and a focus, or a split naming shares - see the README for the shape and the vocabulary). `Ctrl+U` and the Settings Layout row cycle the shipped presets and these names together; a name that is neither of those, or a template that cannot be built, renders `classic` and says why.
